P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Phone number matching latency (database lookup for hashed phone). Notification dispatch to multiple contacts (iteration + async delivery). SMS rate limits (Twilio/Nexmo limits). Location distance calculation (if location sharing enabled).
P.P2_defensibility: E.164 normalization ensures consistency. Hashed phone matching prevents server from seeing plaintext numbers (privacy-friendly). Priority ordering ensures most important contacts notified first. SMS fallback for non-Beacon contacts.
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence in phone normalization and matching (standard practices). High confidence in notification dispatch (async queuing proven pattern). Medium confidence on SMS cost optimization (needs monitoring).
P4_failure_modes: Phone not found in Beacon → SMS fallback may fail if SMS not enabled or user doesn't have phone number (mitigate: allow manual SMS or other contact method)
Multiple users with same phone number → wrong contact matched (mitigate: fuzzy name match, user can manually link)
Status notification fails → contact not notified (mitigate: retry with exponential backoff, user can manually call)
SMS rate limits exhausted → some contacts not notified (mitigate: queue SMS, notify user of delay)
P.P5_backup_plan: If phone matching fails: treat as non-Beacon contact, SMS only. If SMS fails: queue retry. If notification dispatch fails: user can manually call. If SMS not enabled: user sees 'SMS not configured' prompt.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate phone match failure (invalid phone format). Simulate SMS rate limit (inject error). Simulate notification failure (mock delivery service error). Test edge case: contact has no phone or email.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for phone normalization (test vectors for various formats). Integration tests for phone matching (mock user database). Load tests for notification dispatch (1000 contacts notify simultaneously). End-to-end tests for status change → notification flow. SMS delivery confirmation tests.
P.P8_benchmarks: Phone normalization: <100ms. Phone matching: <500ms. Contact list retrieval: <200ms. Status notification dispatch: <2s for all contacts. SMS delivery: >95% within 30s. Contact creation: <1s.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial CONFolder for emergency contacts module

L.L1_legal_considerations: Emergency contacts enable critical communication during crises. PII storage (name, phone, location). SMS notification may be subject to telecom regulation (CAN-SPAM, TCPA). Notification timing critical (delay could cause harm). User must affirmatively consent to contact emergency contacts.
L.L3_consent_requirements: Separate consent for: (1) storing emergency contacts, (2) automatic notification on status change, (3) SMS notification to non-Beacon contacts. Explicit opt-in required for each.
L.L4_liability_notes: Failure to notify emergency contact could expose liability if harm results. Mitigation: clear policy on notification timing, no SLA guarantee (best effort only), user education on reliable contact methods. SMS delivery failures out of Beacon's control (carrier responsibility).

F.F1_cost_considerations: Emergency contact storage: ~500B per contact. SMS: ~$0.01 per message (varies by carrier). At 10k users with 5 contacts each, and 1 status change per event (avg 10 events/year), ~$500/year SMS cost.
F.F2_accounting_considerations: SMS cost scales with event frequency. Variable cost tied to emergency events. Budget for SMS accordingly (could spike during major events).
F.F3_revenue_impact: Emergency notification feature critical to product value prop. May increase user trust and adoption.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Phone numbers hashed before server-side lookup (privacy). Contact list encryption at rest (AES-256). Status notifications encrypted in transit (TLS). SMS unencrypted (out of Beacon's control). Rate limiting on status change notifications (prevent spam/DoS).
S.S2_data_privacy: Contact list visible only to user. Location data (if stored) encrypted. Phone numbers hashed (not plaintext). User can delete contacts. Archive on account deletion.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Phone hash: SHA-256 or similar. Contact data: AES-256 at rest. Notification transport: TLS. SMS: unencrypted (telecom standard).
S.S4_access_control: User sees own emergency contacts only. Contacts do not know they're on user's list (until notification). Status notifications routed only to designated contacts.
S.S5_audit_requirements: Audit log of contact additions/deletions. Audit log of status notifications sent. Audit trail retention: 7 years (legal requirement for telecom).

X.X1_notes: Emergency contacts are critical Beacon feature. Priority ordering (near vs far) is important for evacuation. Hashed phone matching balances privacy with functionality. SMS fallback essential for non-Beacon users. Integration with evacuation system needed (Wave F & H).
X2_open_questions: SMS fallback enabled by default or opt-in? (opt-in is safer, but reduces reach)
Notification frequency limits? (prevent spam if user spam-triggers status changes)
Should emergency contacts see location? (privacy vs safety tradeoff)
Should user confirm before emergency contact notification? (adds friction, but prevents false alarms)
X.X3_related_research: Emergency communication systems. SMS gateway providers (Twilio, Nexmo, AWS SNS). Phone number normalization (libphonenumber). TCPA regulations. Crisis communication best practices.
